apiMessages.content: Plan my first 3 weeks back in the gym. Schedule all the sessions.

content.text: Scheduling a 3-week return-to-lifting ramp: 4x/week upper/lower split (Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat), starting today. Loads are RPE-based, not tied to old maxes — 2 months detrained means jumping straight back to prior weights is how you get hurt. Volume/intensity climb each week; pull-ups reintroduced week 3 once the shoulders/lats are primed.

apiMessages.content:
All 12 sessions scheduled — Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat, 4x/week, through Oct 10.

**Structure:** Lower A (squat) / Upper A (bench) / Lower B (deadlift) / Upper B (press), each with 4-5 accessories.

**Progression:**
- Wk1 (Sep 22–26): 3 sets, RPE 6, ~50-55% of pre-layoff loads
- Wk2 (Sep 29–Oct 3): 4 sets on mains, RPE 7, ~60-65%
- Wk3 (Oct 6–10): mains drop to 4-5 reps, RPE 7-8, ~65-70%; weighted pull-ups reintroduced

Load prescriptions are RPE-based, not fixed weights — you set the actual bar weight day-of based on feel. Don't override RPE 6-7 to hit old numbers early; that's the fastest way to re-injure after a 2-month layoff. Bench Press, Deadlift, and Overhead Press were added to your exercise library (they weren't there before).

The 3-week return-to-lifting plan is fully scheduled — nothing further queued. If you want, I can extend into weeks 4+ (progressing toward heavier singles/doubles), add conditioning days, or start logging nutrition. What's next?
